heard: Half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies. Astronomers once believed our galaxy was the entire universe. Edwin Hubble proved billions of other galaxies existed in the 1920s. Up to 50% of the Milky Way actually came from them. Distant supernova explosions drove this matter across space. These intergalactic currents fed us directly into our galaxy. That cosmic dust eventually built our planet, our sun, and us. It is why half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies.
